location_qualifier: near Cape Esperance, landed as a covering force for the withdrawal
source_locator: R2230: C25080236900 (十四日エスペランス附近に上陸せる矢野大隊); R2225: ch. XV (about 600 replacements ashore near Cape Esperance on 14 January, named the Yano Battalion in the XIV Corps report)
current_activity: landing near Cape Esperance to cover the withdrawal
notes: JACAR 17th Army operations record, vol. 2: on 14 January the 17th Army commander took under his command the Yano Battalion, which had landed near Esperance. Miller, chapter XV, agrees that about 600 replacements were put ashore near Cape Esperance on 14 January 1943 to cover the withdrawal, and that the XIV Corps report names the body as the Yano Battalion. Confidence 0.7 (Japanese official catalog excerpt and US Army official history agree on the day, place and name). The commander’s given name and rank were not copied from a page read.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: holding the west bank of the Bonegi as a delaying force
notes: Miller, ch. XV: on 1 February 1943 the Japanese unit holding the west bank of the Bonegi against the 147th Infantry was a delaying force from the covering battalion which the Japanese had landed on 14 January. That landing is already C12843 (Yano Detachment, 0.7, JACAR and Miller). This Bonegi position is Miller only, so confidence is 0.5.

location_qualifier: Cape Esperance / Kamimbo area, covering force of the last evacuation lift
source_locator: R2230: C25080237200 (撤収し二月八日迄にブーゲンビル島ユレベンタに上陸); R2225: ch. XV (last destroyer lift the night of 7–8 February)
current_activity: covering the last evacuation lift from Cape Esperance
notes: JACAR vol. 2 dates completion of the withdrawal, with evacuees landing at Evrenata on Bougainville, by 8 February 1943. Miller, chapter XV, dates the last destroyer lift to the night of 7–8 February. Confidence 0.5: the two families agree that the evacuation ended that night, but this increment did not copy a sentence that names the Yano Battalion on the last lift, so its presence as the covering force that night is inferred from its 14 January covering role (old value: no end claim; new value: 8 February withdrawal at Kamimbo; reason: the army’s evacuation had ended and a later on-island location was not read).
